title: Wittich (via Widmar): remission-assurance accidental; essential acts are assent, love, refuge-trust
source_text: CXX. In eandem quoque sententiam citavimus Wittichium Professorem Leydensem, qui inter actus fidei salvificae accidentales, & qui fidei tantum corroboratae conveniunt, ponit fiduciam de remissione peccatorum a Deo impetrata. Et observat ad fidei justificantis essentiam, sive rationem formalem, Non requiri fiduciam remissionis peccatorum, sive in praeterito, sive in futuro, sed eam esse effectum fidei magis corroboratae & plenae. Quoniam experientia docet infirmos quosdam fideles revera habere fidem, qui tamen nondum possunt sibi, propter suam imbecillitatem, persuadere, quod habeant vel sint consecuturi remissionem peccatorum. Actus autem fidei essentiales docet esse, assensum tum generalem omnibus revelatis, tum specialem huic veritati, quod Christus sit sufficiens salvator omnibus ad se confugientibus, adeoque etiam mihi, si serio desiderem justitiam, atque ad Christum confugere velim. Deinde amorem Christi syncerum inde orientem. Ac tertio fiduciam qua nobis persuademus, auxilium certum nos accepturos a Christo salvatore in omnibus angustiis & tentationibus, innixi promissionibus factis omnibus ad se confugientibus. Denique distinguit fiduciam illam, per quam acquiescimus in Christo & Deo, tanquam unico fonte & authore salutis, & servatore sufficienti omnibus ad se confugientibus, quam dicit ad fidei essentiam omnino pertinere, a fiducia prout significat persuasionem de remissione peccatorum, sive in praeterito, sive in futuro, qua dicit fidem posse destitui, sed ejusmodi fidem infirmam esse. Quam doctrinam testatur se primum accepisse a praeceptore suo reverendo Widmario Professore Groningano.
pass_a_gloss: In the same opinion we have also cited Wittich, Leiden professor, who among the accidental acts of saving faith — those that suit only corroborated faith — places trust concerning remission of sins obtained from God. And he observes that for the essence, or formal reason, of justifying faith, trust of remission of sins, whether past or future, is not required, but that it is an effect of faith more corroborated and full. Because experience teaches that some weak believers truly have faith who yet cannot yet persuade themselves, because of their weakness, that they have or will obtain remission of sins. But the essential acts of faith he teaches are: assent both general to all things revealed, and special to this truth, that Christ is a sufficient Savior for all who flee to him — and so also for me, if I seriously desire righteousness and wish to flee to Christ; then sincere love of Christ arising thence; and third, trust by which we persuade ourselves we will receive certain help from Christ the Savior in all straits and temptations, leaning on the promises made to all who flee to him. Finally he distinguishes that trust by which we rest in Christ and God as the only fountain and author of salvation and sufficient Savior for all who flee to him — which he says altogether belongs to faith's essence — from trust as it signifies persuasion of remission of sins past or future, of which he says faith can be destitute, but such faith is weak. Which doctrine he testifies he first received from his teacher, the Reverend Widmar, Groningen professor.
pass_b_english: Wittich (Leiden), following Widmar: trust that sins are already remitted is accidental — an effect of strengthened faith, not justifying faith's essence.
Weak believers may truly believe yet be unable to persuade themselves they have or will receive remission.

Essential acts: general assent to revelation; special assent that Christ is sufficient Savior for those who flee to him (including me if I desire righteousness); sincere love of Christ; trust of certain help in trials.
Resting in Christ as sole fountain of salvation is essential; persuasion of past/future remission can be lacking in weak but real faith.
